summary: The frozen history test rejected every pre-registered stock rule: each beat only a small share of random baskets from the same list, and holding every name equally beat every rule and the core. Setup checks and past strength have shown no edge here. The market eased slightly on the latest day after its big rally, and its mood stays stressed with the trend down. All five calls stay neutral with low conviction. Nothing here is expected to beat the index; real money stays in the whole-market plan.
eli5: After a big sprint, the runners slowed to a jog. The brain still does not guess who wins, because guessing did no better than luck before. It watches with pretend money, and the family's real money keeps going into the whole-market basket every week.
letter:
Dear family,

First, real money. Nothing to do today and nothing to sell. This week's buy of the whole-market fund should already be in; if not, put it in. The market gave back a little after its big jump, which is ordinary. Money we may need soon stays safe.

Second, the pretend game. Every stock rule we wrote down in advance lost to baskets picked at random from the same list, so our stock calls stay neutral. Last week's bet lost, so the game stands at two weeks won and two lost, exactly what luck alone would give. This week's bet is early and a little behind.

Third, a lesson. Two won and two lost is a coin. It takes many weeks before a record says anything about skill, so we keep counting and keep our money out of it.

Fourth, what would change our minds: a rule that beats random picks on history and then keeps a paper record ahead of the whole market for at least half a year. Until then we stay patient.

With care, the brain
